From 47cbfe2608314b833ad61a65827d8fb363bc2d2d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yasuaki Torimaru <yasuakitorimaru@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 20:46:34 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] drm/msm/gem: fix error handling in
 msm_ioctl_gem_info_get_metadata()

msm_ioctl_gem_info_get_metadata() always returns 0 regardless of
errors. When copy_to_user() fails or the user buffer is too small,
the error code stored in ret is ignored because the function
unconditionally returns 0. This causes userspace to believe the
ioctl succeeded when it did not.

Additionally, kmemdup() can return NULL on allocation failure, but
the return value is not checked. This leads to a NULL pointer
dereference in the subsequent copy_to_user() call.

Add the missing NULL check for kmemdup() and return ret instead of 0.

Note that the SET counterpart (msm_ioctl_gem_info_set_metadata)
correctly returns ret.

Fixes: 9902cb999e4e ("drm/msm/gem: Add metadata")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Yasuaki Torimaru <yasuakitorimaru@gmail.com>
Patchwork: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/714478/
Message-ID: <20260325114635.383241-1-yasuakitorimaru@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Rob Clark <robin.clark@oss.qualcomm.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_drv.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_drv.c
index ed2a61c66ac9..c7f6d07a5043 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_drv.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_drv.c
@@ -536,6 +536,11 @@ static int msm_ioctl_gem_info_get_metadata(struct drm_gem_object *obj,
 	len = msm_obj->metadata_size;
 	buf = kmemdup(msm_obj->metadata, len, GFP_KERNEL);
 
+	if (!buf) {
+		msm_gem_unlock(obj);
+		return -ENOMEM;
+	}
+
 	msm_gem_unlock(obj);
 
 	if (*metadata_size < len) {
@@ -548,7 +553,7 @@ static int msm_ioctl_gem_info_get_metadata(struct drm_gem_object *obj,
 
 	kfree(buf);
 
-	return 0;
+	return ret;
 }
 
 static int msm_ioctl_gem_info(struct drm_device *dev, void *data,
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file, `drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_drv.c`, to fix two error handling issues in the function `msm_ioctl_gem_info_get_metadata()`.

**Modifications in `drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_drv.c`**:
- Added a NULL check after the `kmemdup()` call. If `kmemdup()` fails (returns NULL), the function now unlocks the GEM object and returns `-ENOMEM`.
- Changed the final return statement from `return 0` to `return ret`. Previously, `ret` held the error code from the size check or `copy_to_user()` failure, but the function always returned 0, ignoring those errors.

**Relationship between the modifications**:
Both changes improve error handling in the same function. The first fix prevents a NULL-pointer dereference by handling memory allocation failure. The second fix ensures that errors from the user-space copy and size validation are correctly propagated to the caller instead of being silently ignored. Together, they guarantee that the function returns an appropriate negative errno on any failure, matching the behavior of its counterpart `msm_ioctl_gem_info_set_metadata()`.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>buf = kmemdup(msm_obj->metadata, len, GFP_KERNEL);</text>
<text>return 0;</text>
Reason:
The kmemdup call can return NULL on memory allocation failure, but no check is performed. This results in a NULL pointer dereference when copy_to_user is later called with buf. Additionally, the function always returns 0 regardless of errors from copy_to_user or size mismatch, causing userspace to believe the ioctl succeeded when it actually failed.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>if (!buf) {</text>
<text>    msm_gem_unlock(obj);</text>
<text>    return -ENOMEM;</text>
<text>}</text>
<text>return ret;</text>
Reason:
The added NULL check ensures that if kmemdup fails, -ENOMEM is returned instead of proceeding with a NULL pointer. Changing the final return from 0 to ret propagates the error code from copy_to_user or size validation (e.g., -EFAULT or -ETOOSMALL) to the caller, so that userspace correctly sees the failure.
